scenario.title: Updates, distribution and stale installed layers
situations: A newer Yoke version is available.
CLI, relay, dashboard and project teaching disagree.
Update cannot find the machine distribution or would replace a source checkout.
scenario.current: Research trace; requirements and source paths need live proof.
questions: How are users first notified of version availability across each mode?
Are component refresh receipts and the source-versus-installed layer version discoverable from one support entry?

lessons.title: Update through the recorded distribution
lessons.need: yoke update reuses the machine distribution origin/channel, reports verified old/new versions and repairs the credential helper. Distribution is not the active control-plane connection. Missing records need explicit distribution selection.
lessons.surface: Install -> upgrade instructions -> CLI/config -> distribution help.

lessons.title: Refresh the stale component, not just the page
lessons.when: An upgrade succeeded but hooks, dashboard or installed project instructions remain old
lessons.need: Distinguish installed CLI, server, resident hook process, relay and tracked project layer. Follow the component-specific status/refresh result; a webpage reload does not replace its serving process.
lessons.surface: Current project orientation warns on older operating-layer receipt; FIRST-USER 6/15 add resident hook/dashboard restart and E checks.

lessons.title: Recognize the source-checkout boundary
lessons.when: An updater refuses a source-bound install
lessons.need: A source checkout is updated through its source process and exact server build, not replaced with packaged wheels. Do not turn a source-maintainer recovery into a general external-user recipe.
lessons.surface: Install/private-fork support limits and updater refusal.
